title: [Feature][1/N] Add KDA RecoverSSM Triton operators
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Add the Ascend GLM KDA RecoverSSM Triton operators. Verification records correction/key/gate data; after sampling, commit reconstructs the accepted recurrent state and compacts convolution history. Each KDA page needs one recurrent checkpoint instead of additional per-draft checkpoints.

Support NPU graphs, with optimized verify, compact and commit kernels for A3/A5. This is part 1/N split from #19133, containing the operators, their tests and required operator documentation in one commit. Model, worker, configuration and PD integration are left to the framework follow-up.

References: original Kimi-K3 RecoverSSM ([vllm#51855](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51855)) and GLM KDA integration ([vllm#61566](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61566)).

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No serving behavior or configuration is enabled by this part. The new operator entry points are exercised directly by the single-operator tests; framework callers and user-facing activation will be added separately.

The historical integrated-model results below remain experimental: generation may differ from ordinary MTP; tokenwise equivalence is not guaranteed. Reduced KDA checkpoint storage does not imply an equivalent reduction in total reserved KV memory.

### How was this patch tested?

The following operator validation is inherited from the earlier integrated version in #19133. The exact extracted operator/test source passed 144 A3 cases and 1280 output comparisons; current-source A5 full-suite validation remains pending after its validation sequence stopped during the commit microbenchmark due to device OOM.

#### Triton operator validation (A3/A5)

1. **Functionality:** GLM KDA verification, accepted-state commit and convolution compaction reduce draft checkpoint storage. Eager and NPU graph execution are covered with H32/H64, K=V=128, BF16/FP16 activations and FP32/BF16 states. Operator documentation and tests are included. Grouped commit uses the configured window, with explicit Q1/Q2/Q4/Q6/Q8 path regressions.
2. **Accuracy:** Against independent FP64 references, each device passed 142 tests and 1260 output comparisons. Every output achieved a 100% element-wise mixed-tolerance pass rate and satisfied its maximum absolute-error limit. The largest errors across both devices were BF16 `3.2176e-03`, FP16 `2.2898e-05` and FP32 `4.1121e-07`. Copy-only results and untouched regions matched exactly. For the same-algorithm stride optimization, all 24 checkpoint comparisons had zero maximum absolute difference.
3. **Performance:** Compared with the same-algorithm baseline `b5326cd6b`, nine alternating graph-timing rounds used recorded strides, B11/B12, L11/L12 and accepted lengths 1/3/6. Commit latency changes ranged from `-5.30%` to `+5.39%` on A3 and `-1.49%` to `+3.62%` on A5; both improvements and regressions are reported. Removing the fixed-window restriction retained identical checkpoints in six Q6 A5 cases; grouped latency changed by `-0.52%` to `+0.21%` against `b7ec33b35`.
4. **Safety:** Shape/dtype/stride, static-window and tile specialization sources were reviewed. With MTP5/Q6, after warmup, all four active kernels recorded zero JIT memory-cache misses during the full GSM8K run, with no new or modified persistent compilation artifacts. **No recompilation was observed in this dataset run.** Write boundaries and untouched regions were checked; nonlinear operands have FP32 assertions, and the context patch is installed only for GLM with RecoverSSM enabled.
